I personally don't think we should care about every V8 flag except those that we explicitly support or we know are very likely to be used in the wild.
That said, this feature is still at stage 3 in the tc39 process, and that would be a good reason for waiting.

Stage 3, not just 4, is the time to ship things, and ideally node wouldn’t even allow unsupported v8 flags to be provided, but it’s certainly an unfortunate situation until the v8 flag is removed or noop’d.

> Stage 3, not just 4, is the time to ship things

That's what we thought, then import assertions were demoted (and I think it also happened to decorators in the past).

@targos true indeed, import assertions is a very unique case (decorators were never stage 3 until their last advancement).

The only times anything's been demoted from stage 3 in the past besides Import Assertions that I recall is Numeric Separators, and once the syntax conflict was addressed, it jumped back up to stage 3 with no changes.
FWIW the proposal will be going for stage 4 next month: https://github.com/tc39/agendas/commit/9a41ec6334554cf8c9fe0992b65e09c8daaefe27
@legendecas Should we continue with this pull request? Or should we wait for the official stage 4 - next month?
It's already shipped in two browsers, so the chance it'll change in a breaking way imo is pretty much zero - for what that's worth.

> @anonrig Should we continue with this pull request? Or should we wait for the official stage 4 - next month?

I support landing the PR when the flag `--harmony-string-is-well-formed` is noop-ed. My concern is that the _stable_ API `util.toUSVString` is broken when the experimental feature is turned off by the flag `--no-harmony-string-is-well-formed`.

Also, I expect that we don't want to use `str.toWellFormed()`, but instead `StringPrototypeToWellFormed(str)`. At that point we might as well just keep the `util.toUSVString` function around, but set it to `StringPrototypeToWellFormed` when the latter becomes available. (Notice that `toWellFormed` [automatically](https://tc39.es/proposal-is-usv-string/#sec-string.prototype.towellformed) converts its **this** argument to a string, so the `` `${arg}` `` trick isn't needed.)
@legendecas Is it a noop now? https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Av8%2Fv8%20harmony-string-is-well-formed&type=code

@ljharb I applied your suggestions but I'm getting the following error:

```
Uncaught TypeError: StringPrototypeToWellFormed is not a function
    at Object.toUSVString (node:util:389:12)
```
It'll need to be imported from primordials in every file it's used in; i can't leave suggestions on lines that aren't diff-adjacent :-/

> It'll need to be imported from primordials in every file it's used in; i can't leave suggestions on lines that aren't diff-adjacent :-/

It's imported but `primordials.StringPrototypeToWellFormed` does not exist.
ah, then that suggests that the flag isn't nooped yet, otherwise i think it would be automatically available?

> ah, then that suggests that the flag isn't nooped yet, otherwise i think it would be automatically available?

`Reflect.ownKeys(String.prototype)` returns `toWellFormed` and `copyPrototype` should work it's magic, but it doesn't - Ref: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/per_context/primordials.js#L229
Hmm, that seems a bug worth fixing - any chance there's something snapshot-related there? i don't know how those work.

I marked the PR as "dont-land", since the V8 update won't be backported.

review_comments: why this change? The primordial already coerces to string, so this is just redundant.

It throws error:

```
❯ out/Release/node test/parallel/test-whatwg-url-custom-searchparams.js
node:internal/url:590
    value = StringPrototypeToWellFormed(value);
            ^

TypeError: String.prototype.toWellFormed called on null or undefined
```
ok, but surely the string null or undefined isn’t what’s desired here - that exception seems like it’s exposing a bug?
That’s because the method takes no arguments, and the primordial operates on the first argument as the receiver. If you use .call on the method it will throw the same.
looks like browser USP stringifies these too, so this is indeed the correct change, it's just a surprising API design :-/ feel free to resolve this.
